concepts.name: Client-server architecture
concepts.summary: Explain that a Postgres server process manages databases and serves client connections, each handled by a separate backend process.

concepts.name: Cluster, database, schema hierarchy
concepts.summary: Distinguish a cluster, the databases within it, and the schemas and tables within each database.

concepts.name: Roles and login privileges
concepts.summary: Understand that users and groups are both roles and that the LOGIN attribute lets a role connect.

concepts.name: Core built-in data types
concepts.summary: Choose among basic types such as integer, text, numeric, boolean, date and timestamptz for simple columns.

concepts.name: Installing and starting Postgres
concepts.summary: Describe how a cluster is initialised and how the server is started and stopped on a system.

concepts.name: Connecting with psql
concepts.summary: Connect to a database using psql with host, port, user and database parameters and run a query.

concepts.name: psql meta-commands
concepts.summary: Recall common commands such as \l, \c, \dt, \d and \q to inspect and navigate a database.

misconceptions.text: A Postgres database and a Postgres server are the same thing.
Roles and users are different kinds of objects in Postgres.
You can query across multiple databases in the same cluster with a simple schema-qualified name.

concepts.name: Serial and identity columns
concepts.summary: Generate surrogate keys using identity columns or sequences and explain why gaps can occur.

concepts.name: Timestamp with time zone
concepts.summary: Store and query timestamps with timestamptz and apply session time zone settings correctly.

concepts.name: Array columns
concepts.summary: Define array columns, index into them, and query them using ANY, containment operators and unnest.

concepts.name: JSONB storage and operators
concepts.summary: Store JSON documents in jsonb and extract or filter values using the arrow and containment operators.

concepts.name: Basic B-tree indexes
concepts.summary: Create a B-tree index on a column to speed up equality and range lookups.

concepts.name: Reading simple EXPLAIN output
concepts.summary: Read an EXPLAIN plan to tell whether a query uses a sequential scan or an index scan.

concepts.name: Granting privileges
concepts.summary: Grant and revoke table and schema privileges to roles to give least-privilege access.

concepts.name: Logical backup with pg_dump
concepts.summary: Take a logical dump of a database and restore it into another database.

misconceptions.text: timestamptz stores the time zone alongside the value.
Creating an index guarantees the planner will use it.

concepts.name: EXPLAIN ANALYZE interpretation
concepts.summary: Compare estimated and actual row counts, timings and buffer usage to find the costly step in a plan.

concepts.name: Multicolumn and partial indexes
concepts.summary: Design composite, partial and covering indexes whose column order and predicates match query patterns.

concepts.name: GIN indexes for JSONB and arrays
concepts.summary: Apply GIN indexes to speed up containment and membership queries on jsonb and arrays.

concepts.name: Transaction isolation levels
concepts.summary: Analyse which anomalies each isolation level permits and choose a level for a workload.

concepts.name: Row-level locking
concepts.summary: Use explicit row locks and diagnose lock waits and deadlocks in concurrent transactions.

concepts.name: Planner statistics and ANALYZE
concepts.summary: Explain how table statistics drive row estimates and how stale statistics produce bad plans.

concepts.name: Join and scan strategies
concepts.summary: Analyse why the planner picks particular scan and join methods for given data sizes and indexes.

concepts.name: Configuration parameters
concepts.summary: Adjust core settings such as shared_buffers and work_mem and know which need a reload or restart.

misconceptions.text: A sequential scan is always slower than an index scan.
Column order in a multicolumn index does not matter.
Read committed isolation gives each transaction a stable snapshot for its whole duration.

concepts.name: MVCC and tuple visibility
concepts.summary: Analyse how row versions, transaction ids and snapshots produce concurrency without read locks and leave dead tuples.

concepts.name: Vacuum and autovacuum tuning
concepts.summary: Evaluate autovacuum behaviour and tune thresholds to control bloat and prevent transaction id wraparound.

concepts.name: Write-ahead log and checkpoints
concepts.summary: Analyse how WAL ensures durability and how checkpoint settings trade recovery time against write load.

concepts.name: Streaming replication
concepts.summary: Analyse primary-standby replication, replication lag and the consistency tradeoffs of synchronous versus asynchronous modes.

concepts.name: Point-in-time recovery
concepts.summary: Evaluate a backup strategy combining base backups and WAL archiving to meet recovery objectives.

concepts.name: Table partitioning
concepts.summary: Judge when and how to partition tables and verify that partition pruning works for queries.

concepts.name: Query diagnosis with statistics views
concepts.summary: Use statistics views and pg_stat_statements to find slow queries, blocked sessions and unused indexes.

concepts.name: Extensions and index types
concepts.summary: Select extensions and index types such as BRIN, GiST or trigram for a given data and access pattern.

misconceptions.text: VACUUM FULL is the normal way to keep tables healthy and should be run regularly.
A streaming replica is a backup that makes point-in-time recovery unnecessary.
Partitioning a table always improves query performance.

concepts.name: Logical replication and zero-downtime migration
concepts.summary: Plan upgrades and schema migrations using logical replication with minimal downtime.

concepts.name: Capacity and workload modelling
concepts.summary: Evaluate connection limits, pooling modes and hardware sizing against a projected workload.

concepts.name: High-availability architecture design
concepts.summary: Design a high-availability topology with automated failover that avoids split brain and meets stated recovery goals.

concepts.name: Planner cost model tuning
concepts.summary: Evaluate and correct planner misestimates using extended statistics, cost parameters and query rewrites.

concepts.name: Sharding and scale-out strategy
concepts.summary: Assess scale-out options such as read replicas, partition-based sharding and foreign data wrappers for a given system.

concepts.name: Security hardening and row-level security
concepts.summary: Create a security design combining authentication rules, TLS, least privilege and row-level security policies.

concepts.name: Custom extension and function design
concepts.summary: Create custom functions, types or extensions where built-in features fall short, weighing maintenance cost.

concepts.name: Incident diagnosis and recovery
concepts.summary: Judge root causes in production incidents such as lock pileups, bloat or replication breakage and choose recovery actions.

misconceptions.text: Adding more connections or a bigger max_connections value increases throughput.
Logical replication copies schema changes and sequences automatically.
Automated failover is safe as long as a standby can be promoted quickly.
